concepts.def: A precise sequence of steps that solves a problem or completes a task, which can be represented in pseudocode or as a flowchart.
Breaking a complex problem into smaller sub-problems, each of which is easier to understand, solve and test separately.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Fundamentals Of Algorithms — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Fundamentals Of Algorithms brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Fundamentals Of Algorithms.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Can binary search be used on an unsorted list?
options: Yes - binary search works on any list because it always checks the middle.
No - binary search relies on the list being sorted so it knows which half to discard; on unsorted data it may throw away the half containing the target.
Yes - bubble sort only ever needs to compare the first two items.
Yes - binary search sorts the list while it searches.

mcqs.q: Does one pass of bubble sort fully sort a list?
options: Yes - binary search sorts the list while it searches.
No - one pass only guarantees the largest unsorted item bubbles to its correct end position; multiple passes are needed until no swaps occur.
Yes - bubble sort finishes after a single pass through the list.
Yes - bubble sort only ever needs to compare the first two items.

mcqs.q: Does abstraction mean making a problem vaguer?
options: No - abstraction removes irrelevant detail while keeping the essential features precise, like the London Underground map keeping stations and connections exact.
Yes - abstraction means adding artistic decoration to diagrams.
Yes - an abstract version of a problem is just a less accurate one.
Yes - binary search sorts the list while it searches.
